# Evidence, open team sheets — what every legal effect lets reach the log about Stat Points

**Generated** by `npm run catalog` (`scripts/local-catalog.mjs`). Do not edit by hand:
`npm run catalog -- --check` fails when this file and a fresh run disagree.
**Format:** `gen9championsvgc2026regmc`, simulator `pokemon-showdown` at `a5df827`.
**Pool:** 293 species, 216 abilities, 510 moves, 166 items, 94 conditions, 25 natures.
**Read with:** `evidence-catalog.md` §1–§2.

## 0. How to read a card

Each effect was put in small battles in the real format, its **templates**. In each, the hidden Pokemon (p2a)
had every Stat Point at 2 except one, set to 0 in one world and 32 in the other. A **change** is a line of the
known side's view that differs between the two worlds, less what the **control** — the same battle without the
effect — changes the same way. An HP line that moves its Pokemon by the same exact amount in both worlds, or by
the same amounts as in the control, only repeats an earlier difference and is dropped. A change is `own` when the
effect printed it (its move, its `[from]` tag, a line naming it) and `modified` when it changed a line something
else printed: a hit that lands harder after Swords Dance. A stat seen only through modified lines is bracketed in
the grid.

Each stat with changes was then rebuilt from each world's log alone by `inferSpreads`, the way
`npm run reconstruct -- --infer p2` rebuilds a replay. **Verdicts:**

| Verdict | Glyph | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| USED | ✓ | given one world's log, the inference removes the other world's spread, which differs only in this stat. Where the control's own lines also tell the worlds apart, an event of the inference must also have read the effect's line and cut the hidden Pokemon |
| UNUSED | ✗ | both worlds rebuild, the real spread survives in each, and neither rules out the other: the log carries the stat and the inference does not tell them apart |
| UNSOUND | ‼ | the real spread was removed in one of the worlds — a defect, first on the work list |
| REBUILD-FAILED | ↻ | not told apart, and a world's log did not rebuild to the end; its first wrong line is listed. Often the same gap: an unused stat leaves the rebuild without a spread that reproduces the line |
| MASKED | ○ | the worlds were told apart, but the control's lines already do that and no event read the effect's own line to cut more: unused, or with nothing left to add — this battle cannot say which |
| ERROR | ! | the rebuild threw |
| UNSTABLE | ~ | the two worlds drew a different number of dice, speed ties aside, so the difference is not only the stat: rebuilt only to check that each world keeps its real spread, which it does |

A stat is judged per role and per mechanism: the worst defect over the templates that showed it through that
mechanism, else the best use. So Gyro Ball's Speed through its damage (M3) and through turn order (M7) are two
verdicts, and one does not hide the other. The grid gives each, bracketed when only a modified line showed it.

The inference checks its own shortcuts as it goes: where one gives another answer than the simulator at the stats
the rebuild is running with, the line is set aside, not trusted. A line set aside can leave a stat UNUSED or
REBUILD-FAILED, never UNSOUND; §2.7 lists every one.

**Outcomes:** CHANNEL — at least one change. NO CHANNEL — the effect acted and changed the log, but nothing it changed
depends on a Stat Point in these battles. NOT SHOWN — no template made it change the log: it failed, or did nothing
these battles could see; the card says which. **Sinks:** `hidden %` an HP figure of the hidden side, `known exact`
one of the known side, `order` two units of a turn swapped, `presence` a line printed in one world only, `names` a
line whose words changed. **Spectator:** how a published replay (channel 0) shows the change — `same`, `as %`,
`hidden` (it shows no change), `absent`. **Mechanisms** are `evidence-catalog.md` §2's, assigned by rule from what
printed the line; `M?` fits none. Roles: `U` user hidden, `T` target hidden, `H` holder hidden, `O` the known side
holds it and acts on the hidden Pokemon, `A` a hand-set battle that varies the hidden Pokemon's ally (p2b) instead.
A hand-set battle may also name its two worlds, or sweep a stat over every value 0–32 and ask about each two
adjacent values the known side's view tells apart; such a row names its pair, `HP 13|14`. A card may carry a
written **Reason** the effect cannot carry a Stat Point on an open sheet, or a **Reason for** one row of it —
`T:Spe` for a verdict row, `read:HP` for a stat its handlers read unseen — which takes that row off the work list;
and a template a choice **the battle overrode** — a lock, a trap, a barred move, a Pokemon that had left — with
why. At most three changed lines per stat are shown. `npm run catalog -- --dump <effect> <role/template> <stat>
<value>` prints the battle behind any row and what the rebuild made of it.

### 2.3 REBUILD-FAILED and ERROR

The first line the rebuild got wrong, as its last round compared it: turns the inference had already pinned are compared on exact HP, so a hidden figure can show exactly here.

None.

Template user-hidden/category-flip: Shell Side Arm compares the hidden Slowbro-Galar's Attack and Special Attack against the known Snorlax's Defence and Special Defence, and the move line names the category it chose: Physical up to Special Attack 26, a coin on the tie at 27 to 29, Special from 30. The two worlds stand either side of the tie, so neither throws the coin.

Template user-hidden/category-sweep: Swept over Special Attack: where the special formula overtakes the physical one, the category the move line names flips, through the coin on the tie.

Template target-hidden/target-category-flip: The known Slowbro-Galar's Shell Side Arm compares its Attack and Special Attack against the hidden Snorlax's Defence and Special Defence: Physical up to Defence 20, a coin on the tie at 21 and 22, Special from 23, which the move line names.

Template target-hidden/target-category-sweep: Swept over the hidden Snorlax's Defence: the known Slowbro-Galar's Shell Side Arm turns Special once the Snorlax's Defence makes the physical formula fall below the special one, which the move line names.

Template target-hidden/target-category-sweep-spd: Swept over the hidden Snorlax's Special Defence: the known Modest Slowbro-Galar's Shell Side Arm is Special while the Snorlax's Special Defence is low and turns Physical once it makes the special formula fall below the physical one, which the move line names.

Reason for sweep:SpA: onModifyMove settles a tie between its two damage estimates with randomChance(1, 2) (data/moves.ts:16228-16240), and at this boundary one world's estimates tie, so the two worlds throw a different number of dice; each keeps its real spread, and the category-flip battle reads the hint's category on both sides of the tie.

Reason for sweep:Def: onModifyMove settles a tie between its two damage estimates with randomChance(1, 2) (data/moves.ts:16228-16240), and at these boundaries one world's estimates tie, so the two worlds throw a different number of dice; each keeps its real spread, and every boundary without a tie is USED.

Reason for sweep:SpD: onModifyMove settles a tie between its two damage estimates with randomChance(1, 2) (data/moves.ts:16228-16240), and at this boundary one world's estimates tie, so the two worlds throw a different number of dice; each keeps its real spread.

Reason for T:Spe: The known user takes the hidden target's stored Speed (transformInto, sim/pokemon.ts:1302), so the copy and its original race at one Speed: a tie the dice settle, which says nothing. The copied Speed is raced against a known pacer instead.

Reason for U:Spe: The hidden user takes the known target's stored Speed (transformInto, sim/pokemon.ts:1302) and keeps none of its own, so the copy and its original race at one Speed: a tie the dice settle, which says nothing.

Template user-hidden/partner-healed: The halved partner is switched into the wisher's slot and healed by half the wisher's max HP, which its percentage then shows.

Template user-hidden/self-healed: Twice halved by Super Fang, the hidden Clefable heals itself at the end of the next turn by the half of its own max HP its Wish stored: 171 max HP prints 74/100 and 201 prints 75/100.

Template user-hidden/self-healed-sweep: Swept over HP: Super Fang's halves and the Wish's half of the Clefable's own max HP each round by the simulator's own rule, so where the healed percentage moves between neighbouring Stat Points depends on both.

Template holder-hidden/priority-race: At full HP Gale Wings gives the hidden Talonflame's Tailwind +1, the priority of the known Weavile's Ice Shard, so the two race: Talonflame's 146 to 178 against Weavile's 152.

Reason for read:HP: onModifyPriority asks whether the holder is at full HP (data/abilities.ts:1590), which its own percentage already says: the Champions display prints 100/100 only at hp === maxhp (Math.floor in getHealth, sim/pokemon.ts:2068), so the gate depends on no Stat Point; the Spe channel is USED.

Template holder-hidden/race-in-disguise: The hidden Zoroark's first-turn lines name its disguise, p2a: Slowking, and the known Arcanine's Extreme Speed then breaks it and |replace| shows who it was: its 125 to 157 against Arcanine's 141 on the first turn.

Template holder-hidden/race-never-unmasked: Nothing breaks the hidden Zoroark's disguise as the hidden Persian, which could have made the same order lines at 135 to 167, so Zoroark's 125 to 157 against the known Arcanine's 141 stays unread.

Reason for O:Spe: The known holder is shown as Mudsdale and no |replace| settles that it was the Illusion user, so its order lines name nobody for certain and are not used; the control, with no disguise, reads the same order.

Reason for H:Spe: The disguised holder's order lines name the Pokemon it poses as (onBeforeSwitchIn, data/abilities.ts:2056-2069); where no later |replace| in its slot settles who switched in, a line naming the disguise is read for neither Pokemon.

Reason for aside: A switch-in on a side with an Illusion user that no |replace| settles could have been the Illusion user posing as the Pokemon shown (onBeforeSwitchIn, data/abilities.ts:2056-2069), so what it showed belongs to neither for certain: each such Pokemon keeps every spread either reading leaves it, and the Illusion user keeps none of the lines.

Template other-hidden/race-the-copy: The known Ditto's Imposter copies the hidden Blastoise across from it on switching in, Speed 98 to 130 included, and Ditto then races the known Gardevoir's 114.

Reason for H:Spe: onSwitchIn transforms the hidden holder into the foe opposite (data/abilities.ts:2116-2123), whose stored Speed it takes (sim/pokemon.ts:1302), so the copy and its original race at one Speed: a tie the dice settle, which says nothing. A hidden Speed a known Imposter copies is raced against a known pacer instead.

Template holder-hidden/second-hit-past-a-substitute: The Mega Kangaskhan's first hit breaks the known Snorlax's Substitute, which shows no number, at every Attack; Parental Bond's second hit, at a quarter of the power, then lands on Snorlax, and its exact HP shows the Attack.

Reason for H:SpA: A second hit shown alone needs a first that prints no number. A Substitute does that for the physical hit, which breaks it at every Attack (H:Atk, USED), but whether Mega Kangaskhan's special hit breaks a Substitute depends on its Special Attack, so the break itself would carry the stat. Here the second hit, at a quarter of the power, adds nothing to what the first hit's line read.

Reason for O:Spe: Parental Bond reads no Speed. The hidden Blastoise's Speed is read by its order against the known Mega Kangaskhan, which narrows it in both worlds; the line this row measures, Blastoise's Splash, is there only when it moves before the two hits knock it out, so no event of its own names it.

Template holder-hidden/heals-on-the-bench: Halved by Super Fang, the hidden Slowbro switches out and heals a third of its max HP on the bench with no line of its own; the switch line that brings it back shows it: 170 and 202 print 82/100 and 83/100.

Template holder-hidden/heals-on-the-bench-swept: Halved by Super Fang, the hidden Slowbro switches out and heals a third of its max HP on the bench with no line of its own; the switch line that brings it back shows it: 170 and 202 print 82/100 and 83/100.

Reason for H:Def: Defence is carried by the physical hit before the switch, not by the heal: onSwitchOut heals a third of the holder's max HP (data/abilities.ts:3834-3835), which reads no Defence.

Template other-hidden/spread-on-both: Halved first, the known holder heals by an eighth of what its spread move dealt both hidden Pokemon together, which its exact HP shows.

Template other-hidden/two-hits: Halved first, the known holder heals by an eighth of what both hits dealt the hidden Pokemon together, which its exact HP shows.

Reason for O:SpD: onAfterMoveSecondarySelf heals the known holder by an eighth of what its hit dealt (data/items.ts:5657-5659); at a fixed HP that heal falls in the same step at every Special Defence the hidden Pokemon's percentage leaves, so telling two values apart needs HP and Special Defence swept together, which no hand-set battle does.

## 6. Conditions

A condition has no battle of its own. Its rows are the changes other effects' battles printed with it in `[from]`.

A line tagged with a condition's name is `[from] <it>`, or one that starts it; a condition that acts through `|cant|` or `-singleturn` (a flinch, Protect) is never tagged, and says nothing here either way.
